input: Repaint the living room accent wall gray

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing the wall's size and current condition (e.g., patching needed, existing dark color) determines how much prep work, primer, and paint are required.
Gray spans a huge spectrum from warm greige to cool charcoal; the specific shade and finish (matte, eggshell, satin) dramatically changes the look and product choice.
A fixed budget affects whether the user buys premium paint, hires help, or does it all themselves with budget supplies.
Whether the user is doing this solo, with helpers, or hiring a professional painter changes the plan, timeline, and tool recommendations entirely.
The deadline or target date affects how the tasks are sequenced — e.g., whether there is time to let primer fully cure or to do multiple coats over several days.
Knowing what tools and materials the user already has (rollers, tape, drop cloths, primer) avoids redundant purchases and shapes the shopping list.
Understanding what a great result looks like to the user — a clean DIY job, a perfectly smooth professional finish, or matching existing decor — sets the quality bar for the whole plan.

gold.taskTitle: Repaint living room accent wall gray
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to repaint one accent wall in their living room a shade of gray.

questions.title: What are the wall's approximate dimensions and current color?
questions.description: Knowing the height, width, and existing paint color helps estimate paint quantity and whether a primer coat is necessary.

questions.title: Which gray tone and paint finish are you picturing?
questions.description: Identifying the preferred shade (light/warm, cool/dark) and finish (matte, eggshell, satin) narrows down the exact product to buy.

questions.title: What is your budget for this project?
questions.description: A clear budget ceiling guides choices on paint brand quality, tool purchases, and whether to hire any help.

questions.title: Will you be painting yourself or hiring a professional?
questions.description: This determines whether the plan focuses on DIY technique guidance or on finding and briefing a contractor.

questions.title: Do you have a target date to have this completed by?
questions.description: A deadline shapes how tasks are sequenced, including drying and curing time between coats.

questions.title: What painting supplies do you already have on hand?
questions.description: Knowing existing tools (rollers, brushes, painter's tape, drop cloths, primer) prevents duplicate purchases and refines the shopping list.

questions.title: What does a successful result look like to you?
questions.description: Understanding the quality bar — e.g., a clean DIY finish, a flawless professional look, or simply complementing existing furniture — sets the standard the whole plan works toward.
